# Sharded Zarr V3: Sentinel-2 {#sec-sharded}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

Zarr V3 added sharding: many small chunks packed into one object, with an
index at one end saying where each chunk's bytes are. Small chunks make
small reads possible; shards keep the object count sane. ESA's EOPF
sample service publishes Sentinel-2 Level-2A products this way, each band
a matrix at 10, 20, 60 m and coarser.

To a reader, a shard is one more level of byte references: a ranged read
of the index, then each chunk is a byte range of the shard file. That is
the same shape as a virtual store, and zaro plans it the same way.

This chapter is here for a second reason. A band is a matrix, and
`m[i, j]` takes a different path through R than `x[i, j, k]`:
`MatrixSubset()`, not `ArraySubset()`. R's source calls the split
"purely an optimization", but it means the element loop exists twice, and
the patch offers the method from both places. These reads exercise the
matrix one.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| file: scripts/05-sharded.R
```

```{r}
res <- book_run("05-sharded.R", live = TRUE)
book_table(res)
```

The third read is a strided one: every tenth pixel of a 4000 x 4000
window, a quick-look. On a lazy array that is still every chunk under the
window, because a compressed chunk is all or nothing. What the plan saves
is, again, the round trips.

```{r}
book_elt(res)
```

::: {.callout-note}
The product URL is under a `tests-output` path on the sample service and
may move. If this chapter shows no results, the script needs a current
product; any Sentinel-2 L2A Zarr from the service will do.
:::
